Resource: FHIR Version: R4B (4.3.0) — base resource: Procedure, unchanged in structure between R4 and R4B

Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. Canonical FHIR ValueSet (required binding): preparation | in-progress | not-done | on-hold | stopped | completed | entered-in-error | unknown. 'stopped' and 'not-done' both matter in emergency care (e.g. resuscitation stopped, intubation attempt failed) — do not default everything to 'completed'.
MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — useful for grouping/reporting but not essential to identify the specific procedure, which lives in Procedure.code.

Description: The specific procedure performed, e.g. CPR, endotracheal intubation, wound dressing, splinting.
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT. FLAG FROM REAL HANDOVER DATA: the source system's procedure_id values (e.g. 'LA17060-7') follow a LOINC Answer-code pattern, not SNOMED CT — LOINC isn't really designed for procedure coding. Reconcile with the vendor on the intended code system before finalizing; if their catalog is genuinely LOINC-based, this ValueSet binding needs to change, or you'll need a translation/mapping layer at ingestion.

Description: The patient the procedure was performed on.
The encounter the procedure was performed in — typically EMPOCEncounter.
When the procedure was performed. Use performedPeriod for anything with a meaningful duration (e.g. ongoing CPR), performedDateTime for a discrete moment (e.g. a single intubation attempt).
Comments: REQUIRED (Min 1..1) AND MUST SUPPORT — timing precision matters as much here as it does for Condition.onset; a resuscitation timeline is frequently reviewed minute-by-minute afterward.
MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..*) — recommended to always populate in practice.

Description: The specific EMT/paramedic/clinician who performed it.
Result of the procedure, e.g. ROSC achieved / not achieved for resuscitation, successful/failed intubation attempt.
Comments: MUST SUPPORT (Min 0..1) — recommended strongly for resuscitation and airway procedures specifically, since the outcome carries real clinical and legal weight, even though it's not forced to Min 1..1 across every procedure type (e.g. a routine wound dressing rarely needs a coded 'outcome').

Description: Any complications arising from the procedure.
Comments: OPTIONAL — not must-support, but worth populating when relevant for clinical/legal completeness.

Description: Anatomical site the procedure was performed on, e.g. wound location for dressing/splinting.
